thread.title: Updated Music-Copyright Law Clears Senate Panel

author: Anne Steele
title: Updated Music-Copyright Law Clears Senate Panel
text:
Published: June 28, 2018 5:46 p.m. ET Share
Songwriters would get paid more as law adapts to digital age Bloomberg News The bill would streamline the way Apple and other streaming music companies pay for the rights to songs.
By Anne Steele
Legislation that aims to revamp an outdated music-licensing system and help songwriters get paid more won the unanimous approval of the Senate Judiciary Committee, paving the way for a full Senate vote on the bill, a version of which has already cleared the House of Representatives.
The Music Modernization Act, or MMA, updates copyright law for the digital age and is the result of unprecedented cooperation between the music industry and the streaming services that have upended how the business earns money.
The Senate bill and the House version, which the House passed in April, 415-0, are widely supported by major music publishers, songwriters and streaming services. “We’re in the age of the Internet, and the laws governing what songwriters are paid are from the age of the player piano,” said Sen. Lamar Alexander, R-Tenn., a co-sponsor of the bill introduced by Sen. Orrin Hatch, R-Utah, in May.
The central part of the bill calls for the creation of a body to administer royalties owed to songwriters by music-streaming services such as Spotify SPOT, +0.27% and Apple AAPL, -0.21% Music. The legislation would streamline the complicated way those services get access to millions of songs and pay for the rights to carry them.
